config.description: 16 kHz mono PCM16 (stereo averaged), DC removal, level normalisation (provisional), relative energy trim (provisional thresholds), no noise reduction
config.review_note: Investigation PPINV001 (experiments/PPINV001/summary.json) on all 128 validated references fixed channel handling, sample rate, resampler, DC removal, sample format and the trim mechanism. Normalisation values and trim thresholds/padding stay PROVISIONAL until representative learner recordings exist.

resample.note: Colab/deployment must reproduce output hashes recorded in processed/<PP>/transformation_log.csv

silence_trim.note: threshold relative to the file's peak sample level (gain-invariant); applied after resampling; endpoint (leading/trailing) trim only

decoding.lossy: NOT DEFINED: learner m4a/AAC decoding must be pinned to a decoder + version when learner recordings exist

decoding_pcm.evidence: all 128 references are PCM16 WAV; exact integer-to-float mapping, tested

decoding_lossy.evidence: no lossy input exists yet; decoder and version must be pinned on real learner files

channel_handling.evidence: PPINV001: L/R correlation min 0.979 (median 0.99995), |RMS diff| <= 0.043 dB, best cross-correlation lag 0 in 128/128, no polarity inversion, average-vs-louder-channel loss <= 0.054 dB (no cancellation), FE001 distance between L/R/average < 3% of frame spread. Averaging is safe and symmetric; a per-file guard (corr >= 0.9 and cancellation loss > -3 dB) is logged for future inputs

target_sample_rate_hz.evidence: energy above 8 kHz: median 0.007%, max 1.24% of total; speech-band coverage; standard MFCC rate; mobile-deployment realistic; soxr HQ deterministic, duration error < 0.032 ms, sample counts exact

resampler.evidence: byte-identical repeated runs, finite output, peak change within +/-0.27 dB

sample_format.value: float64 internal, PCM16 LE WAV derived files
sample_format.evidence: round-half-even, clip count logged; 0 clipped samples on references

dc_offset_removal.evidence: measured |DC| <= 0.00104 FS; mean subtraction is deterministic and harmless

normalization.evidence: FE001 (C1..C13, no energy) is gain-invariant except in near-silent frames hitting the 1e-10 log floor (58/128 files show a gain effect > 0.01 before trimming; see summary.feature_sensitivity). Normalisation therefore matters only through floor/threshold behaviour and cross-device level differences, which cannot be judged without learner recordings. Reference-only facts: peak -1 dBFS gains -1.0..+9.1 dB; RMS -20 dBFS gains -10.0..+4.4 dB with post-gain peaks <= -0.97 dBFS (no clipping)

silence_trim_method.value: frame RMS endpoint trim, 10 ms frames, threshold relative to peak
silence_trim_method.evidence: relative threshold is gain-invariant (tested); references are already edited masters (leading quiet 20-330 ms, trailing 0-440 ms at -40 dBFS), so the mechanism must not over-trim: min FE001 frames after rel-40 trim = 37, no file below 30 frames

silence_trim_threshold_db.evidence: on references -30/-40/-50 dB remove median 15%/8%/0% of samples; learner recordings will contain more silence and noise, so the threshold must be set on representative learner audio

silence_trim_pad_ms.evidence: as above; padding cannot restore audio already cut in the masters

noise_reduction.evidence: no justification from the reference domain; enabling it later requires a new PP id and learner evidence
